problem: WGS-84 is a datum (a coordinate system with an ellipsoid, an origin and a realisation), not an ellipsoid. Calling the shape itself 'WGS-84' blurs the two.
fix: 'The standard shape is an ellipsoid of revolution, the ellipsoid of the WGS-84 datum, with semi-major axis a = 6 378 137 m and flattening f = 1/298.257223563.'

problem: 'Satellite orbits and GPS coordinates are expressed on this ellipsoid' is loose: a satellite position is a point in space fixed by a frame (ECEF/ECI), not a point on the ellipsoid surface. Only the ground coordinates use the ellipsoid.
fix: 'GPS coordinates are expressed on this ellipsoid, and satellite positions are given in the Earth-fixed frame tied to it.'

problem: 'The bearing of the station from the aircraft differs from the bearing of the aircraft from the station by 180°' is exact only for magnetic or rhumb-line bearings. For true great-circle bearings the two differ by 180° plus the convergence of the meridians, which is not negligible on long legs.
fix: '...differs by 180° for magnetic or rhumb-line bearings; on long great-circle legs the true bearings differ by 180° plus the convergence of the meridians.'

problem: σ is described as 'the 1-sigma position error along each line of position', but the error that matters is measured perpendicular to the line of position; along the line the position is unconstrained. This contradicts the sentence two paragraphs above saying uncertainty is largest along each line.
fix: 'σ is the 1-sigma position error perpendicular to each line of position (the same for both lines).'
